thread:
maria: Starting caldera11b onboarding — ran overnight int4 quant on canary pool. quick summary: quality spot-checks look fine, but we hit a couple OOMs and a p95 latency spike on batch=8

raj: yup saw that. two failures at ~02:13 and ~02:44 UTC. both OOMs on nodes with mixed warm/cold sessions. stack shows KV alloc blowup then CUDA OOM

emily: fyi evals: rouge/bleu-ish proxy metrics unchanged vs fp16 for our 1k-sample prompt set. slight degradation on long-form coherence (max_new_tokens heavy)

sam: can you paste the relevant logs? also which binpack/alloc policy used?

maria: logs (trimmed):
```
[02:13:21] alloc_slot: kv_cache reserve 1.2G -> 3.9G
[02:13:21] cuda: memoryError: out of memory while allocating 4096 bytes
[02:13:21] runtime: active_prefetchers=6, batch_size=8, max_new_tokens=1024
```
config we used:
```
model: caldera11b
quant: int4
batch_size: 8
max_new_tokens: 1024
prefetch_workers: 6
kv_shrink_threshold: 0.2
```

raj: root cause hypothesis: int4 reduced model weights ok but increases transient alloc churn from prefetch + kv cache when max_new_tokens is large. fragmentation triggers OOM for larger batches

luis: agreed. seen similar on other models — int quant often reduces steady-state footprint but increases number of small CUDA allocations which fragment GPU heap. lowering concurrent prefetchers or reducing max_new_tokens helps

emily: performance numbers from overnight canary (median across 50 runs):
- fp16, b=4, max_new=512: p50=48ms/token, p95=120ms/token
- int4, b=4, max_new=512: p50=45ms/token, p95=130ms/token
- int4, b=8, max_new=1024: p50=42ms/token, p95=320ms/token (OOMs in 4% runs)

sam: ok action items I suggest:
1) change default onboarding profile for caldera11b: max_new_tokens=256 for int4 canary runs
2) reduce prefetch_workers to 2 for canary int4
3) add kv_shrink after each sample over 512 tokens (temporary patch)
4) fallback to fp16 on OOM + record metric for quality degradation

maria: drafted a small patch for 1+2, putting on canary now. patch note:
```
profiles:
  - name: caldera11b-int4-canary
    quant: int4
    max_new_tokens: 256
    prefetch_workers: 2
    batch_defaults: {batch_size: 4}
```
CI run kicked off by ci-bot: https://ci.internal/redwood/6278901234

ci-bot: Canary test matrix started (caldera11b-int4-canary). 12 trials queued. will post results in thread when done. :robot_face:

raj: also +1 to adding a simple microbenchmark for allocation churn (alloc/free rate) as part of onboard smoke. helps detect frag-prone configs early

luis: i'll add that microbenchmark to the onboarding harness today. suggests tracking small-alloc-rate and peak-heap-frag-ratio

emily: side note — quality regression we saw for very long generation (>2k tokens) remains for int4 vs fp16. not catastrophic but worth surfacing to product if we keep int4 in heavy longform workloads

sam: good flag. for now we gate int4 by workload type: "short/interactive" allowed, "longform" defaults to fp16 unless customers opt-in with caution

maria: canary patch deployed to 2 nodes. will update in ~30m with metrics. thanks all

luis: thanks — saving logs & diffs to /artifacts/6278901234-caldera-onboard.tar.gz

emily: ping if any regressions on rouge/coherence after canary runs, i'll run the 1k noise-resilient eval set

maria: update 30m later: canary finished 12/12 trials, no OOMs, p95 down to ~140ms/token at b=4 max_new=256. leaving canary profile as default for now and opening follow-up for microbenchmark + longform policy

sam: awesome. follow-up ticket: INF-3421 "caldera11b int4 onboarding - allocation microbenchmark + longform gating"

maria: closing thread, will attach eval artifacts to ticket. :thumbsup:
